text.title: Nvidia slide extends S&P losing streak; cybersecurity lifts Nasdaq; oil, gold sink
text.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.2% for a fifth straight losing day and closed at its lowest since July, while the Dow dropped 1.1%. The Nasdaq rose 0.4% and the Russell 2000 gained 0.5%. Nvidia's post-earnings drop weighed on the broad market, a cybersecurity rally helped tech, and oil and metals fell sharply.

drivers.t: Nvidia closed lower after earnings, dragging the S&P 500 to a fifth straight loss, and the Dow fell more than 500 points. Headlines say the company's attempt to move past the Jensen Huang exit did not reassure investors, and the sell-off also hit neocloud names CoreWeave and Iren.
Palo Alto Networks jumped after hours after raising its outlook, citing the threat environment and demand ahead. That helped tech stocks, with the Nasdaq up 0.4% and the technology sector up 0.3%.
WTI crude fell 3.1% to $82.00 as the market focused on abundant supply more than on Middle East conflict. The energy sector lost 3.3%.

drivers.h: Gold and metals hit yearly lows
drivers.t: Gold fell 3.6% to $3,725.60. Metals futures set new lows for the year, with gold and silver dragged down in part by a slide in copper. Natural gas rose against the broader commodity retreat.

Treasury yields settled mixed on hawkish Fed commentary and demand for safer assets amid equity volatility. The 10-year yield slipped 3 bp to 5.07% and the 2-year was unchanged at 4.80%. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed growing unease about the inflation outlook.
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the targeted range, after selling more shares than planned on strong demand. It is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday.

earnings.t: Shares rose after hours as the company raised its outlook, pointing to the current threat environment and demand it sees ahead.
